english: Where did the cows go? Others drove them off early. Did my father fight against them? He fought against them at the fold and died. Now who protects us? My son, you protect us. Now you are the man. I am small and I am afraid. Your father still trembled and stood.

How many men did they kill, brother? They killed seven of our men and grandfather. Now where are the women? They drove off the women and children together with the cattle. Did they seize sister too? They seized her too. We saw her weeping. Now we will follow them. We will follow them at dawn; we will lay our dead on the ground in order today.

Warriors carried off the herdsman's grandson by the river. His grandfather searched for him nine days. Then he came to their village. He saw the grandson carrying water at the door. To his master he gave silver. The master took it and released the slave. Grandfather and grandson returned home, and she poured tears of joy.

Lady, they carried off the gold and the wool. I will go after them to the enemy village. Do not go. They will kill you. Our daughter is captive. I will pay their price. Who sees gold and does not release her? Now the gods see this. Now go and pour milk by day.

The king of the town carried off the old man's daughter. The old man brought him gold and silver. The king did not take it and drove the old man away. The old man sat by the sea and called Dyeus. Dyeus heard him. A plague killed the warriors and cattle for nine days. Then the king released the daughter and gave the old man gifts.
uncertain: ǵr̥h₂n̥tés 'of the old men' vs 'of the town'

english: I carried gold to the king. I have now given him silver and cows. He did not respect my gift, he smiled and turned away. My daughter weaves in his house. Now I carry the gold back. Father Dyeus, look on my grief.
